Summary  
Today I continued working on Task 29, which focuses on building a FastAPI service for interacting 
with both local and hosted Large Language Models (LLMs). The main focus was on improving the 
service structure, separating configuration from application logic, using a shared model-calling 
function, integrating OpenAI-compatible clients, and making the service easier to configure and 
evaluate. 
A major part of today's work involved understanding the architecture of the FastAPI service. Both 
/chat/local and /chat/hosted endpoints follow the same request and response contract 
while using the shared ask_model() function for model inference. This helped reinforce the 
concept of separating the API layer from the underlying model provider and inference logic. 
I also reviewed how th

erence. This helped reinforce the 
concept of separating the API layer from the underlying model provider and inference logic. 
I also reviewed how the application selects between local and hosted inference. The local 
configuration uses Ollama as the model runtime, while the hosted configuration uses an OpenAI-
compatible API provider. The provider URL, API key, and model name are controlled through 
environment variables so that the application code does not need to be changed when switching 
configurations. 
Another important part of today's work was understanding the difference between an API client, 
API endpoint, provider, model, and local model runtime. I also reviewed how Ollama allows 
locally running LLMs to expose an OpenAI-compatible API, which makes it possible to use the 
same Python client and shared inference logic for both local and hosted models.

same Python client and shared inference logic for both local and hosted models. 
I additionally reviewed model quantization concepts in relation to the local Llama 3.2 3B model. I 
understood that the application itself does not perform quantization; instead, the local 
model/runtime provides the selected model variant. The local Ollama model was reviewed in 
relation to the Q4_K_M quantization format. 
Finally, I worked on the project documentation and evaluator setup. I prepared the structure for a 
README.md file containing the correct Uvicorn command, project structure, installation 
instructions, environment configuration, API endpoints, testing instructions, and local model 
requirements. I also continued reviewing the unit tests and the PEFT/LoRA documentation.

Task 1 – FastAPI Service Refactoring 
 Reviewed and refined the FastAPI application structure. 
 Used app/main.py as the main application module. 
 Kept separate endpoints for local and hosted inference: 
 /chat/local 
 /chat/hosted

 Used a shared ask_model() function for the actual model-calling logic. 
 Learned how shared logic reduces duplication between endpoints. 
 Kept the API request and response structure consistent across both endpoints. 
 Used Pydantic models for request and response validation. 
 Used ChatRequest to validate incoming messages. 
 Used ChatResponse to define the response structure. 
 Added a /health endpoint for checking whether the FastAPI application is responding.

 Reviewed the architecture of the local and hosted inference flow. 
 Understood that the FastAPI endpoint acts as the application/API layer.

The shared model call uses the standard chat-completion structure:

Task 4 – Environment-Based Configuration 
 Reviewed the use of .env for application configuration. 
 Configured separate variables for local and hosted inference. 
 Local configuration includes: 
 LOCAL_BASE_URL 
 LOCAL_API_KEY 
 LOCAL_MODEL 
 Hosted configuration includes: 
 HOSTED_BASE_URL 
 HOSTED_API_KEY 
 HOSTED_MODEL 
 Used python-dotenv to load environment variables. 
 Reviewed why API keys should not be hardcoded inside source code. 
 Learned how environment-based configuration makes it easier to change providers or 
models without modifying the FastAPI implementation. 
 Reviewed the use of override=True when loading .env values.

Task 6 – Model Quantization 
 Reviewed the concept of model quantization for local LLM inference. 
 Inspected the local Llama 3.2 3B model information through Ollama. 
 Reviewed the Q4_K_M quantization format. 
 Learned that quantization reduces the numerical precision used to represent model 
parameters.

 Understood that lower-precision model variants can reduce memory requirements and make 
local inference more practical. 
 Learned that the application code itself does not perform the quantization. 
 Understood that Ollama provides/manages the selected model variant. 
 Learned that Q4_K_M should not simply be described as every parameter being a basic 
INT4 value because it is a block-based quantization format with different precision 
characteristics.

 Reviewed error handling for local and hosted model requests. 
 Used try/except around downstream model calls. 
 Returned HTTP status code 502 Bad Gateway when the FastAPI service encounters an 
upstream model/provider failure. 
 Learned why 502 is appropriate for failures involving a downstream model service or 
provider.

 Reviewed the testing structure under the tests/ directory. 
 Reviewed tests/test_ask_model.py. 
 Focused testing around the shared ask_model() function. 
 Continued preparing the remaining unit-test work for the refactored service. 
 Learned the importance of testing shared model-calling logic separately from the API

pytest

 Focused on documenting the concepts clearly so they can be explained during technical

Task 10 – README and Evaluator Setup 
 Prepared a README.md structure for the Task 29 project. 
 Added instructions for running the FastAPI application. 
 Used the correct Uvicorn command according to the project structure:

uvicorn app.main:app --reload 
 Documented the main application URLs: 
 API: http://127.0.0.1:8000 
 Swagger UI: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs 
 Health check: http://127.0.0.1:8000/health

 Added dependency installation instructions. 
 Added .env configuration guidance. 
 Added API endpoint descriptions. 
 Added example request and response structures. 
 Added local Ollama model requirements. 
 Added pytest commands for running the tests. 
 Added information about the PEFT/LoRA documentation.

Today's main learning was that building an LLM application is not only about calling a 
language model. A reliable LLM service also requires clear separation between the API layer, 
model-calling logic, provider configuration, model runtime, error handling, testing, and

and hosted endpoints consistent while allowing the underlying provider to change through
